page.overview:
Who is Tar-Elendil?

Tar-Elendil was the fourth King of Númenor, succeeding his father Tar-Amandil. He was considered to be a master of lore and a notable scholar.

His oldest child was Silmariën, a daughter, and his second child was Isilmë, another daughter. Silmariën would have become Queen according to the principle of "full cognatic primogeniture". However, the laws dictating succession at the time followed rather the principle known as "agnatic primogeniture", preventing women from ruling. Consequently, his third child and oldest son, Tar-Meneldur succeeded him.

Tar-Elendil was the direct ancestor of all subsequent Kings of Númenor through his son. From the time of the reign of Tar-Elendil, the Númenóreans began to make voyages to Middle-earth. It was in SA 600 that Vëantur, the Captain of the King's Ships, sailed from Númenor to Middle-earth for the first time. He surrendered the Sceptre in SA 740 and died in the year 751 of the Second Age, at the age of 401.

The name Elendil is a Quenya word meaning "Friend of Elves", from the word elen ("elves") and ndil ("friend, devoted to").
